events.title: Six-Day War Begins
events.description: Israel launched preemptive airstrikes against Egyptian air forces, beginning the Six-Day War against Egypt, Jordan, and Syria. Within six days Israel captured the Sinai Peninsula, Gaza Strip, West Bank, East Jerusalem, and the Golan Heights.
events.significance: The war dramatically redrew the map of the Middle East and its territorial and political consequences continue to shape the Arab-Israeli conflict today.

events.title: Assassination Attempt on Robert F. Kennedy
events.description: Shortly after midnight, Senator Robert F. Kennedy was shot at the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles by Sirhan Sirhan, moments after winning the California Democratic presidential primary. He died the following day, June 6.
events.significance: Kennedy's death, coming two months after Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination, deepened the turmoil of 1968 and altered the course of the US presidential race.

events.title: Apple II Goes on Sale
events.description: The Apple II, designed primarily by Steve Wozniak and marketed by Steve Jobs, went on sale in the United States as one of the first mass-produced personal computers with color graphics.
events.significance: The Apple II helped launch the personal computer industry and made computing accessible to homes, schools, and businesses.

events.title: Marshall Plan Announced
events.description: US Secretary of State George C. Marshall, speaking at Harvard University's commencement, outlined a program of American economic aid to help rebuild war-devastated Europe.
events.significance: The Marshall Plan provided billions of dollars in aid, supported Western Europe's postwar recovery, and became a cornerstone of US Cold War policy.

events.title: Birth of Adam Smith (baptized)
events.description: Scottish economist and philosopher Adam Smith was baptized on this date in Kirkcaldy, Scotland; his exact birth date is unknown. He later authored The Wealth of Nations (1776).
events.significance: Smith is regarded as the father of modern economics, and his ideas about free markets and the division of labor remain foundational to economic thought.
